title: Sparsepipe: Sparse Inter-operator Dataflow Architecture with Cross-Iteration Reuse
problem: Sparse Tensor Algebra applications are limited by data movement between operators. Prior work focuses only on intra-operator reuse within single operations, missing inter-operator reuse opportunities at the application level.
motivation: Exploiting inter-operator data reuse can significantly improve performance and data efficiency of sparse tensor algebra applications.
method: The paper represents sparse tensor algebra applications as data dependency diagrams (showing which operations pass data to each other). This reveals where data from one operation can be reused by another—both as direct hand-offs between operations and across repeated iterations of the algorithm. Sparsepipe captures these opportunities using an execution strategy called OEI dataflow (Output-stationary-Element-wise-Input-stationary: keeping outputs in place while inputs flow in a specific order). The hardware implements this by arranging its memory and data paths to keep reused data nearby, minimizing expensive data movement.
key_novelty: The key insight is recognizing that sparse tensor algorithms can reuse the same data across multiple iterations instead of reloading it each time.
contributions: Discovery of two unexplored inter-operator reuse opportunities: producer-consumer reuse and cross-iteration reuse
Sparsepipe sparse dataflow architecture supporting inter-operator reuse
Experimental validation achieving 19.82× speedup vs CPU and 1.77× vs ideal sparse accelerators

metrics.speedup: 19.82× vs CPU, 4.65× vs GPU, 1.77× vs ideal sparse accelerator

primary_theme: Sparse tensor dataflow optimization through inter-operator reuse
